clue.text: Has to be embraced by a stunner

definitions.note: a stun gun from science fiction, here a noun for the device that stuns

indicators.note: something embraced by another is held inside it, so these letters go within the other piece

parts.note: a means per, as in five pounds a head
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is told they must be hugged by a beautiful person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' means 'for each', as in 'ten pence a go'. 'Stunner' looks like a beautiful person but is the sci-fi weapon set to stun.
explanation.definitionFit: A phaser is the Star Trek ray gun that can be set to stun, so it is literally a device for stunning.

clue.text: Wild craze to import domestic office furniture item

indicators.note: to import is to bring something inside, so one piece takes in the other
wild letters run free and are rearranged

parts.note: a den is a study or private room at home, an office in the house

explanation.surface: A fashion mania brings in a piece of home-office furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' gives CREZA, and 'to import' takes in the den.
explanation.definitionFit: A credenza is a sideboard or low cabinet commonly found in offices for storing files.

clue.text: Smart girl dismissing knight

indicators.note: dismissing sends one piece away, so it is removed from the word

parts.note: chick is informal slang for a girl
K is an abbreviation for knight, as in KBE

explanation.surface: A stylish young woman turns away a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic describes something stylishly elegant, which is the sense of smart as well-dressed.

clue.text: Certainly hurry to consume whisky in former days

parts.note: yes is an emphatic agreement, certainly

indicators.note: to consume is to take in, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: to tear is to rush along
rye is a kind of whiskey distilled from rye grain

explanation.surface: Someone affirms that rushing to drink whisky is what people did long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to consume' makes TERYEAR. Rye is the American and Canadian grain whiskey.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesteryear means the past or times gone by, a literary way of saying long ago.

clue.text: Former priest? Hears cracks about that

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the other piece
a word that cracks breaks apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A one-time cleric hears confessions and cracks under the strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former' reads as 'one-time' but is the definition: one who forms. 'cracks' rearranges HEARS around P, the priest; 'that' points back to the priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaper is someone or something that forms or moulds, a literal reading of former as one who forms.

clue.text: Hairs and swellings left and right in different places

indicators.note: different places says the letters are each moved to a spot other than where they started
in here begins the phrase saying each letter goes to a new position within the word

parts.note: blisters are swellings of the skin filled with fluid

explanation.surface: Hairs and blisters crop up all over the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in different places' moves the L of BLISTERS to stand after the T and the R to stand after the B, so left and right trade sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristles are short stiff hairs, as on a brush or a stubbly chin.

clue.text: One may draw wages in foreign shores

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
foreign suggests strange and altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: hire is payment for work, wages

explanation.surface: Someone may earn their pay abroad on distant coasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' rearranges the shores, and 'in' places the wages after the first S. 'draw' means pull a cart, not sketch or earn.
explanation.definitionFit: A shire horse is a big draught breed bred to pull ploughs and drays.

clue.text: Theatre in Spain to feel discontented

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A repertory company playing in Spain is unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: To repine is to fret or complain, a literary verb for being unhappy with one's lot.

clue.text: Almost all concubines hurry

indicators.note: almost all of a word drops its final letter

parts.note: a harem is the group of wives and concubines in a household

explanation.surface: Nearly every concubine is in a rush.
explanation.definitionFit: To hare is to run very fast, like the animal, so it means to rush.

clue.text: Thought to expend money after employment

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase: something that has been put to use, second-hand

indicators.note: to expend is to spend and so give away, here the money leaves the word

parts.note: mused means thought, pondered
M is an abbreviation for money, as in M1 and M3 measures of money supply

explanation.surface: Someone considered spending cash once they had a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thought' is MUSED, and 'to expend' spends its M, the money. The definition reads as a time phrase but describes goods already put to use.
explanation.definitionFit: Used goods are second-hand, having already served a previous owner.

clue.text: Quiet year in unusual city post — one won't work for dictator

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
unusual signals the letters are put in a strange new order

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A posting in a strange city: one employee refuses to serve a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges CITY POST; PY goes 'in'. 'dictator' is not a tyrant but someone dictating letters: this typist works from written copy instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A copy typist types from written drafts, unlike an audio or shorthand typist taking dictation.

clue.text: Good African currency's ready for younger relative

parts.note: the rand is the currency of South Africa, with the possessive S
on means ready or going ahead, as in 'the game is on'

explanation.surface: A sound South African currency is ready for a junior family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandson is the son of one's child, a relative two generations below.

clue.text: Reliable course to produce music for film

parts.note: sound means reliable, as in a sound investment
a track is a course for racing or running

explanation.surface: A dependable route is the way to make a film's music.
explanation.definitionFit: A soundtrack is the recorded score accompanying a movie.

clue.text: Annual return adopted by bank on only a few occasions

indicators.note: something adopted by another is taken into it, so it goes inside

parts.note: to rely on is to bank on, depend on
AR is the abbreviation for annual return, a yearly company filing

explanation.surface: A company's yearly filing is taken up by a bank only now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarely means seldom, happening on few occasions.

clue.text: University blocking national memorial?

indicators.note: a piece blocking another sits in its way, inside it

parts.note: state means national, as in a state funeral

explanation.surface: A university obstructs a national monument.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is one kind of memorial, hence the question mark marking an example.

clue.text: Keen to research place that breeds debts

parts.note: a stud is a farm for breeding horses
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debt

explanation.surface: Someone eager to investigate a breeding farm full of unpaid bills.
explanation.definitionFit: Studious describes a person devoted to study and learning.

clue.text: Greek god giving that girl endless chaos

parts.note: her refers to a female, that girl

indicators.note: endless means losing the final letter

parts.note: a mess is disorder, chaos

explanation.surface: A Greek deity gives a girl unending turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermes is the messenger of the Olympian gods in Greek mythology.

clue.text: Working quietly to block debatable space mission

indicators.note: to block is to get in the way, so these letters stand inside the other piece

parts.note: a moot point is one open to debate
on means working, as a machine that is on
sh is a call to be quiet

explanation.surface: Working silently to halt a contested space project.
explanation.definitionFit: A moonshot was a lunar launch; it now also means any ambitious venture.

clue.text: Stigma involving Queen creates tense situation

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a stain on one's name is a stigma
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Disgrace involving the monarch makes for a fraught atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: Strain is tension or pressure, the condition of a fraught situation.

clue.text: Better to keep son wretched?

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: better as an adjective for recovered from illness means cured

explanation.surface: Is it better to keep a son who is miserable?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as a comparison but is 'recovered', CURED.
explanation.definitionFit: Cursed can mean damnable or wretched, as in 'this cursed weather'; the question mark flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Angel hurries up to catch Paternoster's opening

indicators.note: to catch is to grab hold, so one piece takes the other inside
in a down clue, up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: hares means hurries along

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An angel rushes to take up the Lord's Prayer at its start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns HARES into SERAH, and 'to catch' puts P inside. Paternoster is the Lord's Prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraph is one of the highest order of angels.

clue.text: Slow mover, old, is tucking into sweet cake

indicators.note: tucking into means pushing inside, so these letters go within the other

parts.note: a torte is a rich sweet cake

explanation.surface: A slow old person is eating a sweet cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' reads as eating but means going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The tortoise is proverbially slow, as in the fable of the race with the hare.

clue.text: Mountain guide initially hesitant, coming in after French climbing

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so this letter goes inside the other piece
in a down clue, climbing means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: après is French for after

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter

explanation.surface: A mountain guide, at first reluctant, enters after a French climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns APRES into SERPA, and H comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are a Himalayan people famous for guiding and portering on Everest expeditions.

clue.text: Tabloid gala, a thing of sparkle and glitz

definitions.text: a thing of sparkle and glitz

parts.note: the Mirror is a British tabloid newspaper
a ball is a gala dance

explanation.surface: A tabloid newspaper throws a gala, all glitter and glamour.
explanation.definitionFit: A mirror ball is the rotating globe of tiny mirrors that throws sparkles across a disco floor.

clue.text: Middle of plot on American soil

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece
the middle of a four-letter word is its central two letters

explanation.surface: The centre of an American plot of soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Loam is fertile soil of clay, sand and humus.

clue.text: Fat American backed 50% of diet

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: US is short for United States, so American

indicators.note: fifty percent of a word is half its letters, here the back half

explanation.surface: An overweight American supported half of a diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Suet is the hard fat around animal kidneys, used in cooking.

clue.text: Judge sports referee should get a change of scene

parts.note: ump is short for umpire, an official in cricket, tennis and baseball

explanation.surface: A judge says the referee should be moved elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A jump in film or narrative is an abrupt cut from one scene to another.

clue.text: Melon and peanut dished up with cola

indicators.note: food dished up is served in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Melon and nuts served with a fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The cantaloupe is a variety of melon with orange flesh.
